newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Eurobourses buoyant, sterling hits 4 yr high.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurobourses buoyant, sterling hits 4 yr high.

text.p: European shares were significantly firmer on Friday, boosted by a seventh consecutive record close on Wall Street, and the pound sterling touched a four-year high against the dollar.

The dollar was steady on the mark and yen ahead of U.S. industrial production data (expected at 1415 GMT) but was taking a back seat to the pound, which continued to rally, fuelled by speculation of higher British interest rates.

In New York The Dow Jones industrial average closed above 6,300 points for the first time overnight, energised by the latest figures on U.S. inflation. It closed up 38.76 points at 6,313.00, matching an unbroken string of highs set in February.
In London shares climbed to the day's best levels in late morning bolstered by a firmer tone in both futures and government bond markets.
But traders said the market could have reached its peak, and many were pondering when Wall Street's rally may finally peter out and domestic interest rates would next be raised.

"We're all expecting and waiting for Wall Street to consolidate and it's giving us a reason to hold off buying." said one head of equity sales. "We would like to see just how well our market can tolerate a U.S. consolidation."
The same British interest rate predictions which helped sterling were weighing on the equity market following a sharp rise in retail prices announced on Thursday.
"The mood the market has got itself into about interest rates, we're going to see a continuation of the jitters," said Panmure Gordon Strategist Ian Williams.
In Paris French shares started with a big one percent increase, establishing a fresh year-high for the CAC-40 index, and stocks continued to strengthen.
Dealers said the market was supported by Wall Street as well as by a new contract high in French bond futures.
One riser was carmaker Renault, which jumped 2.23 percent to 122.90 francs after reporting good sales figures.
The French index rise takes shares back to early 1994 levels. The life high, at 2,360.98, was reached on February 2, 1994.

It was a similar story in Frankfurt, where German shares were trading at around record levels, just shy of what dealers described as the psychologically important 2,800 point level. The market was supported by the strong dollar, which is good for German exports, and volumes were high, dealers said.
Speculation of mergers or takeovers in the banking sector fuelled much of the trade, with Commerzbank among volume leaders, they said.
On the foreign exchange front sterling was the focus. It touched fresh four-year highs, just short of $1.67, on predictions of higher British rates before falling back slightly.

"People now do hold the view that interest rates in the U.K. are going to be moving upwards as opposed to rates everywhere else which remain relatively ambivalent," said Chris Tinker, chief treasury economist at Standard Chartered.
Analysts said U.S. October industrial production and capacity utilisation numbers out later in the day should confirm the view that the U.S. economy is heading for a soft landing.
"They (the numbers) should show some more falls which again reinforce the view that U.S. rates are on hold," said Julia Jessop, economist at Nikko Europe.
CURRENCIES AT 1200 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5073 marks and 111.24 yen compared with 1.5096 marks and 111.31 yen late in Europe on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1200 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares had risen 27.9 points to 3,954.0.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index gained 18.76 to 2,236.94.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 14.42 at 2,791.43.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed lower at $379.85 an ounce compared with $382.50 at the London close on Thursday.
